ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Peter writes the word KANGAROO on a see-through piece of glass, as seen on the right. What can he see when he first flips over the glass onto its back along the right-hand side edge and then turns it about $180^{\circ}$ while it is lying on the table?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the initial figure above, on the transparent glass sheet, “KANGAROO” is written normally from left to right. Below there are five candidate figures A–E, showing different text forms after flipping/rotating; among them, E shows that the text still maintains the left-to-right order of KANGAROO, but the letter shapes are flipped vertically. Reasoning: First flip along the glass right-hand edge to the back side, which is equivalent to looking at the words on the transparent glass from the back side, obtaining a left-right mirror image. Next, the glass is placed flat on the table and rotated 180°, that is, a half-turn rotation in the plane. A left-right mirror image plus a 180° rotation has a combined effect equivalent to making the original word into an up-down mirror image, so the letter order is still KANGAROO, but each letter is upside down. Comparing with the options, the one that fits this effect is E.

raw_record.question_text: After Peter flips the see-through glass over along its right-hand edge and then rotates it 180° while it is lying on the table, how will the word KANGAROO appear?

method.method_draft: First read the image: the starting glass shows the word KANGAROO normally, and the answer row gives five candidate transformed appearances labeled A–E. Then use the text instruction in order: flipping a see-through glass over along its right-hand edge makes the writing be viewed from the back, producing a left-right mirror image. Next, rotating the glass 180° while it lies on the table applies an in-plane half-turn. The composition of a left-right mirror followed by a 180° rotation is equivalent to a top-bottom mirror of the original word: the letter order stays KANGAROO, but the letters are vertically reflected. Compare this predicted appearance with the choices; option E is the one showing KANGAROO in the same left-to-right order with vertically flipped letter shapes, so choose E.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：上方的初始图中，透明玻璃片上从左到右正常写着“KANGAROO”。下方有五个候选图形 A–E，展示不同的翻转/旋转后文字形态；其中 E 显示的文字仍保持 KANGAROO 的左右顺序，但字母形状呈上下翻转。推理：先沿玻璃右-hand edge 翻到背面，相当于从背面看透明玻璃上的字，得到左右镜像。接着玻璃平放在桌上旋转 180°，即在平面内做半周旋转。左右镜像再加 180°旋转，合成效果等价于把原字做上下镜像，所以字母顺序仍是 KANGAROO，但每个字母上下颠倒。与选项比较，符合这一效果的是 E。

method.CoT_qualify_0: 推理链整体正确，先描述图像再推理，符合多模态顺序要求；其变换分析与方法草稿一致，最终选 E 与标准答案一致。视觉 claim 基本可由图像验证：初始图为正常的 KANGAROO，选项 E 对应保持左右排列但字母上下翻转的形态。可微调之处是避免说“每个字母”都明显上下颠倒，因为 O 等对称字母外观不变；可改为“整体文字呈上下镜像，非对称字母表现为上下翻转”。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct transformation-composition route: model each physical action as a geometric transformation, compose them, then match the resulting word to the image choices.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the initial normal word KANGAROO on the glass and inspect the five visual answer choices, especially identifying which option preserves the word order while flipping the letter shapes vertically.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the stated sequence of operations: first flip the see-through glass over along its right-hand edge, then rotate it 180° while it is lying on the table.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: A back-side view through transparent material gives a mirror reversal; a 180° planar rotation reverses both horizontal and vertical directions. Composing these gives a vertical reflection of the original word, matching option E.
